text:
sara: FYI I started onboarding NyxLite5b (hybrid Llama/Mistral family) into Dedicated. Ran our proj-order exporter + int4 fast kernels and saw a consistent QA/rerank quality regression vs fp16 baseline. Short repro + observations below.

raj: paste the eval command and one failing sample pls

sara: repro (eval harness):
```
./eval/run_eval.sh --model nyxlite5b-int4 --suite qa,rerank --bs 12 --seed 21
```
Failing QA sample (truncated):
"""
Q: What should the user do if invoice shows duplicate charge?
A_expected: Ask to confirm last 4 digits + initiate refund flow, owner = billing-team
A_observed: repeats partial steps, suggests wrong owner (support-agent-42), lower factuality
"""

mei: did you test fp16 export without proj reorder to isolate quant vs packing?

sara: yes. fp16 matches baseline. Regression only when int4 + proj-order re-packing + our kernel-packed head layout used.

jon: by proj-order re-packing you mean the converter permutes q/k/v into interleaved [head_major] layout for our fused kernels, correct?

sara: correct. converter does reshape->transpose->pack into [num_heads, head_dim] interleave. Hypothesis: Nyx training used nonstandard q/k/v packing so our pack mixes head slices across q/k/v and breaks cross-head phase coherency.

raj: watch tokenizer edgecases. Nyx tokenizer uses NFKC normalizer and merges ZWJ emoji clusters differently from our default. If kv-cache assembly or eos/pad handling shifts indices, attention can address wrong positions on long contexts.

sara: token diff for the prompt head aligns, but long-thread examples show pad/eos offset on some conversions. Example snippet: 
```
# fp16 ids near divergence:  431  12  900  999  2
# int4 packed ids:          431  12  900 1000  2  <- 999->1000 at pad boundary
```

mei: interesting. could be two independent problems: a) weight-layout shuffle changing attention; b) pad/eos handling shifting kv indices. Both can degrade QA/rerank, but layout will also show early-prefix logit diffs.

jon: quick check: run the int4 binary but tell runtime to interpret projections in source order (no runtime re-map). If the regression vanishes, the converter packing is to blame.

sara: running now:
```
export REDWOOD_RUNTIME_FLAGS=PROJ_READ_MODE=SOURCE
./serve_local.sh --model nyxlite5b-int4 --port 9155 --no-autobatch
```

ci-bot: deploy-check: port 9155 started, health ok, p95 89ms (local), queued eval job.

mei: preliminary: with PROJ_READ_MODE=SOURCE the QA answers match baseline for ~88% of cases. Early-prefix next-token logits L2 also drop from ~7e-3 to ~2e-4. So major signal is proj-order mismatch.

raj: good repro. Two engineering tracks: 1) converter: add per-layer proj-layout fingerprint (simple checksum of packed q/k/v strides + sample dot-products) and skip repack when fingerprint deviates; 2) runtime: add shim remap that can reorder per-head slices at load-time to match source ordering when needed (avoid mass re-exports).

jon: for short-term, expose converter flag --preserve-proj-order to emit weights without re-packing. We'll need to measure perf delta but it's fine for onboarding.

mei: follow-up: even with shim there is a small residual regression on long-thread rerank lists that correlates with emoji/soft-hyphen cases. I suspect tokenization normalization + pad assembly into kv-cache still causes occasional index shifts. I'll reproduce a failing long-thread and drop artifacts.

sara: token mismatch snippet I found in failing long thread: 
```
# baseline tokens: ... 2103  77  4321  2
# packed export:    ... 2103  77  4322  2  <- single id bump after ZWJ cluster
```

raj: action items:
- sara: open PR with (A) converter fingerprint + --preserve-proj-order flag, (B) add failing long-thread samples into /eval/artifacts/nyxlite5b/ with token diffs
- jon: implement runtime remap shim (use per-head slice permutation P so that P @ W_packed == W_source), add unit test for perf (<3% p95 penalty target)
- mei: add eval guard: compute per-token next-token logits L2 over first 64 tokens between fp16 and new exports; fail onboarding if mean L2 > 1e-3 on >5% of samples. Also add a kv-cache pad alignment test that replays long contexts with emoji/soft-hyphen sequences.

jon: note: we should also include a converter check to ensure exported header records tokenizer_normalization (NFKC/NFD) and fail if runtime tokenizer != header. That will catch these ZWJ/emoji normalization mismatches earlier.

sara: will upload artifacts and link PRs. Thanks all :thumbsup:

ci-bot: ticket created: #ONB-3901 "NyxLite5b proj-order packing + tokenizer kv-cache drift" assigned to sara/jon/mei, priority P2.
